Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

1	"""Merkle-tree aggregation of W-OTS keys: a few-times signature scheme.
2	
3	A :class:`MerkleSigner` generates ``2 ** height`` W-OTS key pairs up front and
4	commits to every public key in a Merkle tree. The tree root is the single
5	long-term public key; each signature spends one leaf (one W-OTS key pair) and
6	carries the authentication path from that leaf to the root. Only the standard
7	library is used. Public keys and signatures have a versioned binary wire
8	format via ``to_bytes`` / ``from_bytes`` (the signature codec is constrained
9	by the corresponding :class:`MerklePublicKey`). A :class:`MerkleProof`
10	bundles one public key and one signature for independent transport, and a
11	:class:`MerkleBatchProof` does the same for several signatures of the same
12	public key; :meth:`MerkleProof.verify_bound` and
13	:meth:`MerkleBatchProof.verify_bound` additionally bind such proofs to the
14	receiver's expected public key and, optionally, an explicit leaf-index
15	selection. The top-level :func:`multiproof_encode` /
16	:func:`multiproof_verify` pair compresses several signatures of the same
17	public key further into one deterministic proof whose shared authentication
18	nodes are deduplicated into a canonical node set;
19	:func:`multiproof_verify_bound` additionally binds such a proof to the
20	receiver's expected public key and, optionally, an explicit leaf-index
21	selection. :func:`multiproof_select` re-emits a chosen subset of a verified
22	multiproof's leaves as a fresh standalone v1 multiproof — using only the
23	source proof, its messages and the expected public key, with no access to
24	the original signatures or any private key. :func:`multiproof_merge` is
25	the union counterpart: it combines the leaf sets of several verified
26	multiproofs into one fresh v1 multiproof from the source proofs, their
27	messages and the expected public key alone. :func:`multiproof_expand` is
28	the inverse of :func:`multiproof_encode`: it restores a verified
29	multiproof to an ordinary :class:`MerkleBatchProof` of standalone
30	:class:`MerkleSignature` values, again from the source proof, its
31	messages and the expected public key alone. Signer
32	state can be persisted explicitly with
33	:meth:`MerkleSigner.checkpoint` /
34	:meth:`MerkleSigner.from_checkpoint`; the checkpoint contains every private
35	key and is protected only by a SHA-256 checksum against accidental
36	corruption, so callers must store it securely. Alternatively,
37	:meth:`MerkleSigner.from_seed` derives the whole leaf tree deterministically
38	from a 32-byte secret seed, and such a signer can be persisted compactly
39	with :meth:`MerkleSigner.seed_checkpoint` /
40	:meth:`MerkleSigner.from_seed_checkpoint` — a separate versioned 109-byte
41	format that stores the seed instead of every private key and is likewise
42	plaintext secret material.
43	
44	Every signing and verification entry optionally accepts a keyword-only
45	``context``: when omitted (or given as an empty value) the message is
46	hashed exactly as the unbound baseline and existing v1 serialised bytes
47	verify unchanged; when given, the same ``bytes``/``bytearray``/``str``
48	(UTF-8 encoded) context must be supplied to both sides or verification
49	fails.
50	"""

165	def _validate_context(context: Any) -> bytes:

167	
168	    ``None`` and an empty ``bytes``/``bytearray``/``str`` both mean
169	    "no context" and normalise to ``b""``. Any other type raises
170	    ``TypeError``; a ``str`` is encoded as UTF-8.
171	    """
172	    if context is None:
173	        return b""

175	        return bytes(context)
176	    if isinstance(context, str):
177	        return context.encode("utf-8")

182	    """Bind ``message`` to ``context`` for the W-OTS message digest.
183	
184	    ``context`` must already be normalised by :func:`_validate_context`.
185	    The empty context passes ``message`` through untouched, so the
186	    no-context path hashes exactly as the unbound baseline and existing
187	    signatures stay byte-for-byte identical. With a non-empty context the
188	    domain separator, both length-prefixed fields and the message are hashed
189	    by :func:`wots._signing_digits` as one unambiguous byte string, so the
190	    same message under two contexts produces two incompatible signatures.
191	    """
192	    if not context:

194	    message_bytes = _as_bytes(message)

197	        + len(context).to_bytes(4, "big")
198	        + context
199	        + len(message_bytes).to_bytes(4, "big")
200	        + message_bytes
201	    )

225	        _SEED_ELEMENT_DOMAIN
226	        + bytes((w, height))
227	        + leaf_index.to_bytes(4, "big")
228	        + chain_index.to_bytes(4, "big")
229	        + seed
230	    ).digest()

233	def _derive_seed_keys(
234	    seed: bytes, w: int, height: int
235	) -> tuple[tuple[WOTSPrivateKey, ...], list[bytes]]:
236	    """Re-derive every private key and leaf hash for a seed-derived signer."""
237	    b, l1, l2 = _params(w)
238	    chains = l1 + l2
239	    private_keys = []
240	    leaves = []
241	    for leaf_index in range(1 << height):
242	        elements = tuple(
243	            _seed_element(seed, w, height, leaf_index, chain_index)
244	            for chain_index in range(chains)
245	        )
246	        private_keys.append(WOTSPrivateKey(w=w, elements=elements))
247	        endpoints = tuple(_chain_walk(element, b - 1) for element in elements)
248	        leaves.append(_leaf_hash(w, endpoints))
249	    return tuple(private_keys), leaves

255	    height = _validate_height(public_key.height)
256	    _, l1, l2 = _params(w)
257	    return w, height, l1 + l2

328	@dataclass(frozen=True)
329	class MerkleSignature:
330	    """Frozen Merkle signature: leaf index, W-OTS signature, auth path.
331	
332	    ``auth_path`` lists the sibling nodes from the leaf level up to the level
333	    just below the root; every node is 32 bytes.
334	    """
335	
336	    index: int
337	    wots_signature: tuple[bytes, ...]
338	    auth_path: tuple[bytes, ...]
339	
340	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
341	        if (
342	            isinstance(self.index, bool)
343	            or not isinstance(self.index, int)
344	            or self.index < 0
345	        ):
346	            raise ValueError("index must be a non-negative integer")
347	        _validate_nodes("wots_signature", self.wots_signature)
348	        _validate_nodes("auth_path", self.auth_path)
349	
350	    def to_bytes(self, public_key: MerklePublicKey) -> bytes:
351	        """Serialise to the versioned v1 wire format as ``bytes``.
352	
353	        The signature carries no parameters of its own, so ``public_key``
354	        supplies — and constrains — them: the encoding stores the key's ``w``
355	        and ``height``, and the signature must match them (index below
356	        ``2 ** height``, as many W-OTS elements as ``w`` has chains, and an
357	        authentication path exactly ``height`` nodes long). The layout is the
358	        8-byte magic ``b"PQAMSIG\\0"``; one byte each for the version (1),
359	        ``w`` and ``height``; the index and the W-OTS element count as 2
360	        big-endian bytes each; the path count as 1 byte; then every signature
361	        element followed by the authentication path from the leaf level
362	        upwards, 32 bytes each. Encoding is deterministic. A wrong
363	        ``public_key`` type raises ``TypeError``; a signature inconsistent
364	        with the key (or corrupted by bypassing the frozen constructor)
365	        raises ``ValueError``.
366	        """
367	        if not isinstance(self, MerkleSignature):
368	            raise TypeError("to_bytes must be called on a MerkleSignature")
369	        if not isinstance(public_key, MerklePublicKey):
370	            raise TypeError("public_key must be a MerklePublicKey")
371	        w, height, chains = _signature_params(public_key)
372	        index = self.index
373	        if isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int) or index < 0:
374	            raise ValueError("index must be a non-negative integer")
375	        if index >= (1 << height):
376	            raise ValueError("index is out of range for the public key's tree height")
377	        _validate_nodes("wots_signature", self.wots_signature)
378	        _validate_nodes("auth_path", self.auth_path)
379	        if len(self.wots_signature) != chains:
380	            raise ValueError("wots_signature length does not match the chain count")
381	        if len(self.auth_path) != height:
382	            raise ValueError("auth_path length does not match the tree height")
383	        return (
384	            _SIGNATURE_MAGIC
385	            + bytes((_SIGNATURE_VERSION, w, height))
386	            + index.to_bytes(2, "big")
387	            + chains.to_bytes(2, "big")
388	            + bytes((height,))
389	            + b"".join(self.wots_signature)
390	            + b"".join(self.auth_path)
391	        )

393	    @classmethod
394	    def from_bytes(cls, data: Any, public_key: MerklePublicKey) -> "MerkleSignature":
395	        """Parse ``to_bytes()`` output back into a :class:`MerkleSignature`.
396	
397	        ``public_key`` constrains the expected parameters: the encoded ``w``
398	        and ``height`` must equal the key's, the index must be below
399	        ``2 ** height``, the element count must equal the chain count for
400	        ``w`` and the path count must equal ``height``. ``data`` must be
401	        ``bytes`` or ``bytearray`` and ``public_key`` a
402	        :class:`MerklePublicKey`; other types raise ``TypeError``. A bad
403	        magic, an unknown version, a parameter mismatch, a wrong count, an
404	        out-of-range index, truncation or trailing data raises ``ValueError``
405	        and no instance is returned.
406	        """
407	        if not isinstance(public_key, MerklePublicKey):
408	            raise TypeError("public_key must be a MerklePublicKey")
409	        if not isinstance(data, (bytes, bytearray)):
410	            raise TypeError("signature data must be bytes or bytearray")
411	        data = bytes(data)
412	        w, height, chains = _signature_params(public_key)
413	        if len(data) < _SIGNATURE_HEADER_BYTES:
414	            raise ValueError("signature encoding is truncated")
415	        if data[:8] != _SIGNATURE_MAGIC:
416	            raise ValueError("bad signature magic")
417	        if data[8] != _SIGNATURE_VERSION:
418	            raise ValueError(f"unsupported signature version: {data[8]}")
419	        if data[9] != w:
420	            raise ValueError("encoded w does not match the public key")
421	        if data[10] != height:
422	            raise ValueError("encoded height does not match the public key")
423	        index = int.from_bytes(data[11:13], "big")
424	        element_count = int.from_bytes(data[13:15], "big")
425	        path_count = data[15]
426	        if index >= (1 << height):
427	            raise ValueError("index is out of range for the public key's tree height")
428	        if element_count != chains:
429	            raise ValueError("element count does not match the chain count")
430	        if path_count != height:
431	            raise ValueError("path count does not match the tree height")
432	        expected = _SIGNATURE_HEADER_BYTES + (element_count + path_count) * ELEMENT_BYTES
433	        if len(data) < expected:
434	            raise ValueError("signature encoding is truncated")
435	        if len(data) > expected:
436	            raise ValueError("trailing data after the signature encoding")
437	        offset = _SIGNATURE_HEADER_BYTES
438	        wots_signature = tuple(
439	            data[offset + i * ELEMENT_BYTES : offset + (i + 1) * ELEMENT_BYTES]
440	            for i in range(element_count)
441	        )
442	        offset += element_count * ELEMENT_BYTES
443	        auth_path = tuple(
444	            data[offset + i * ELEMENT_BYTES : offset + (i + 1) * ELEMENT_BYTES]
445	            for i in range(path_count)
446	        )
447	        return cls(index=index, wots_signature=wots_signature, auth_path=auth_path)

450	@dataclass(frozen=True)
451	class MerkleProof:
452	    """Frozen, self-contained bundle of one Merkle public key and one signature.
453	
454	    Unlike :class:`MerkleSignature` (whose wire format needs the
455	    corresponding key separately), a proof carries the
456	    :class:`MerklePublicKey` that constrains its :class:`MerkleSignature`, so
457	    it can be transported on its own and verified with :meth:`verify`.
458	    :meth:`verify_bound` additionally binds the proof to the receiver's
459	    expected public key and, optionally, an explicit leaf-index selection.
460	    The proof stores no message and is a pure serialisation container: it
461	    offers neither authentication nor encryption of the wrapper itself.
462	    """
463	
464	    public_key: MerklePublicKey
465	    signature: MerkleSignature
466	
467	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
468	        if not isinstance(self.public_key, MerklePublicKey):
469	            raise TypeError("public_key must be a MerklePublicKey")
470	        if not isinstance(self.signature, MerkleSignature):
471	            raise TypeError("signature must be a MerkleSignature")
472	        if not _signature_matches_key(self.signature, self.public_key):
473	            raise ValueError("signature is not consistent with the public key")
474	
475	    def to_bytes(self) -> bytes:
476	        """Serialise to the versioned v1 proof wire format as ``bytes``.
477	
478	        The layout is the 8-byte magic ``b"PQAMPRF\\0"``; one version byte
479	        (1); the public-key and signature lengths as 4 big-endian bytes each;
480	        then the existing v1 encodings of the public key and of the signature
481	        constrained by that key, in that order. Encoding is deterministic: the
482	        same proof always produces the same bytes.
483	        """
484	        if not isinstance(self, MerkleProof):
485	            raise TypeError("to_bytes must be called on a MerkleProof")
486	        key_bytes = self.public_key.to_bytes()
487	        signature_bytes = self.signature.to_bytes(self.public_key)
488	        return (
489	            _PROOF_MAGIC
490	            + bytes((_PROOF_VERSION,))
491	            + len(key_bytes).to_bytes(4, "big")
492	            + len(signature_bytes).to_bytes(4, "big")
493	            + key_bytes
494	            + signature_bytes
495	        )

497	    @classmethod
498	    def from_bytes(cls, data: Any) -> "MerkleProof":
499	        """Parse ``to_bytes()`` output back into a :class:`MerkleProof`.
500	
501	        ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray``; anything else raises
502	        ``TypeError``. The embedded public key is recovered first and then
503	        constrains the signature. A bad magic, an unknown version, a length
504	        field that is out of bounds or disagrees with the actual content,
505	        truncation, trailing data, an invalid nested encoding, or a signature
506	        inconsistent with the key (wrong parameters or counts) raises
507	        ``ValueError`` and no half-valid object is returned.
508	        """
509	        if not isinstance(data, (bytes, bytearray)):
510	            raise TypeError("proof data must be bytes or bytearray")
511	        data = bytes(data)
512	        if len(data) < _PROOF_HEADER_BYTES:
513	            raise ValueError("proof encoding is truncated")
514	        if data[:8] != _PROOF_MAGIC:
515	            raise ValueError("bad proof magic")
516	        if data[8] != _PROOF_VERSION:
517	            raise ValueError(f"unsupported proof version: {data[8]}")
518	        key_length = int.from_bytes(data[9:13], "big")
519	        signature_length = int.from_bytes(data[13:17], "big")
520	        key_end = _PROOF_HEADER_BYTES + key_length
521	        signature_end = key_end + signature_length
522	        if key_length == 0 or signature_length == 0:
523	            raise ValueError("a length field must not be zero")
524	        if key_end > len(data) or signature_end > len(data):
525	            raise ValueError("proof encoding is truncated")
526	        if signature_end < len(data):
527	            raise ValueError("trailing data after the proof encoding")
528	        public_key = MerklePublicKey.from_bytes(data[_PROOF_HEADER_BYTES:key_end])
529	        signature = MerkleSignature.from_bytes(
530	            data[key_end:signature_end], public_key
531	        )
532	        return cls(public_key=public_key, signature=signature)

534	    def verify(self, message: Any, *, context: Any = None) -> bool:
535	        """Verify the embedded signature against the embedded public key.
536	
537	        Accepts ``bytes``/``bytearray``/``str`` exactly like
538	        :func:`merkle_verify`, to which this call delegates; it returns
539	        ``True`` only for the message that was actually signed. The proof
540	        itself carries no message and cannot authenticate its own origin.
541	
542	        ``context`` is keyword-only and optional: ``None`` (the default) and
543	        an empty value both mean "no context" and verify legacy unbound
544	        signatures; any other ``bytes``/``bytearray``/``str`` (``str`` encoded
545	        as UTF-8) must match the signing context exactly, else the signature
546	        fails to verify. A context of any other type raises ``TypeError``.
547	        """
548	        return merkle_verify(
549	            message, self.signature, self.public_key, context=context
550	        )
551	
552	    def verify_bound(
553	        self,
554	        message: Any,
555	        *,
556	        public_key: Any,
557	        index: Any = None,
558	        context: Any = None,
559	    ) -> bool:
560	        """Verify the signature and bind the proof to an expected key/leaf.
561	
562	        First requires ``public_key`` to equal the public key embedded in the
563	        proof value by value (``w``, ``height`` and ``root``), then runs the
564	        exact verification of :meth:`verify` — ``message`` is checked with
565	        :func:`merkle_verify` against the embedded signature, accepting
566	        ``bytes``/``bytearray``/``str`` (a ``str`` is encoded as UTF-8). No
567	        wire format changes, no new objects, no randomness and no state are
568	        involved.
569	
570	        ``context`` is keyword-only and optional and follows the same rules
571	        as :meth:`verify`: ``None``/empty means no context, while a non-empty
572	        context must be the one used at signing; the wrong context makes the
573	        bound check return ``False``, and a context of a wrong type raises
574	        ``TypeError``.
575	
576	        ``public_key`` must be a :class:`MerklePublicKey`; any other type
577	        raises ``TypeError``. ``index=None`` imposes no constraint on the
578	        leaf selection. An explicit ``index`` must be a non-boolean integer
579	        equal to the signature's leaf ``index``: a value that is not an
580	        integer at all raises ``TypeError``, while a boolean, a negative or
581	        out-of-range value, or one unequal to the signature index returns
582	        ``False``. Missing or mistyped embedded fields (including values
583	        corrupted by bypassing the frozen constructor), and any message,
584	        signature or public-key mismatch return ``False`` without leaking
585	        any other exception.
586	        """
587	        if not isinstance(public_key, MerklePublicKey):
588	            raise TypeError("public_key must be a MerklePublicKey")
589	        context_bytes = _validate_context(context)
590	        if index is not None:
591	            # ``bool`` is a subtype of ``int``, but a boolean is not an
592	            # acceptable leaf selection: it falls through to the structural
593	            # checks below and returns ``False``.
594	            if not isinstance(index, int):
595	                raise TypeError("index must be an integer")
596	        try:
597	            embedded_key = self.public_key
598	            signature = self.signature
599	            if not isinstance(embedded_key, MerklePublicKey):
600	                return False
601	            if not isinstance(signature, MerkleSignature):
602	                return False
603	            if (
604	                public_key.w != embedded_key.w
605	                or public_key.height != embedded_key.height
606	                or public_key.root != embedded_key.root
607	            ):
608	                return False
609	            if not merkle_verify(
610	                message, signature, embedded_key, context=context_bytes
611	            ):
612	                return False
613	            if index is None:
614	                return True
615	            signature_index = signature.index
616	            if (
617	                isinstance(index, bool)
618	                or isinstance(signature_index, bool)
619	                or not isinstance(signature_index, int)
620	                or index < 0
621	                or index >= (1 << embedded_key.height)
622	                or index != signature_index
623	            ):
624	                return False
625	            return True
626	        except Exception:
627	            # A bypass-constructed proof may carry arbitrary field objects
628	            # whose access or comparison raises anything; the bound check
629	            # reports every such malformed structure as ``False``. External
630	            # argument type errors were raised before this block.
631	            return False

638	        index = signature.index
639	        wots_signature = signature.wots_signature

677	@dataclass(frozen=True)
678	class MerkleBatchProof:
679	    """Frozen bundle of one Merkle public key and several of its signatures.
680	
681	    The batch generalises :class:`MerkleProof`: every
682	    :class:`MerkleSignature` in ``signatures`` is constrained by the same
683	    :class:`MerklePublicKey`, so the whole batch travels as one
684	    self-contained object and verifies with :meth:`verify`.
685	    :meth:`verify_bound` additionally binds the batch to the receiver's
686	    expected public key and, optionally, an explicit leaf-index selection.
687	    ``signatures`` must be a non-empty tuple whose leaf indices are strictly
688	    increasing (hence unique). The batch stores no messages and is a pure
689	    serialisation container: it offers neither authentication nor
690	    encryption of the wrapper itself.
691	    """
692	
693	    public_key: MerklePublicKey
694	    signatures: tuple[MerkleSignature, ...]
695	
696	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
697	        _validate_batch_fields(self.public_key, self.signatures)
698	
699	    def to_bytes(self) -> bytes:
700	        """Serialise to the versioned v1 batch wire format as ``bytes``.
701	
702	        The layout is the 8-byte magic ``b"PQAMBAT\\0"``; one version byte
703	        (1); the public-key length as 4 big-endian bytes; the signature
704	        count as 2 big-endian bytes; the complete v1 encoding of the
705	        public key; then, in tuple order, each signature's length as 4
706	        big-endian bytes followed by its existing v1 encoding constrained
707	        by that key. Encoding is deterministic: the same batch always
708	        produces the same bytes. Fields corrupted by bypassing the frozen
709	        constructor raise ``TypeError``/``ValueError`` instead of
710	        producing a malformed encoding.
711	        """
712	        if not isinstance(self, MerkleBatchProof):
713	            raise TypeError("to_bytes must be called on a MerkleBatchProof")
714	        _validate_batch_fields(self.public_key, self.signatures)
715	        if len(self.signatures) > _MAX_BATCH_SIGNATURES:
716	            raise ValueError("the signature count does not fit in 2 bytes")
717	        key_bytes = self.public_key.to_bytes()
718	        parts = [
719	            _BATCH_PROOF_MAGIC,
720	            bytes((_BATCH_PROOF_VERSION,)),
721	            len(key_bytes).to_bytes(4, "big"),
722	            len(self.signatures).to_bytes(2, "big"),
723	            key_bytes,
724	        ]
725	        for signature in self.signatures:
726	            signature_bytes = signature.to_bytes(self.public_key)
727	            parts.append(len(signature_bytes).to_bytes(4, "big"))

736	        ``TypeError``. The embedded public key is recovered first and then
737	        constrains every signature. A bad magic, an unknown version, a
738	        zero public-key length or signature count, a length field that is
739	        out of bounds, truncation, trailing data, an invalid nested
740	        encoding, a signature inconsistent with the key, or indices that
741	        are not strictly increasing raises ``ValueError`` and no
742	        half-valid object is returned.
743	        """
744	        if not isinstance(data, (bytes, bytearray)):
745	            raise TypeError("batch proof data must be bytes or bytearray")
746	        data = bytes(data)
747	        if len(data) < _BATCH_PROOF_HEADER_BYTES:
748	            raise ValueError("batch proof encoding is truncated")
749	        if data[:8] != _BATCH_PROOF_MAGIC:
750	            raise ValueError("bad batch proof magic")
751	        if data[8] != _BATCH_PROOF_VERSION:

912	    :meth:`sign_selected`, :meth:`sign_selected_with_checkpoint`,
913	    :meth:`sign_selected_with_auth_state`,
914	    :meth:`sign_with_checkpoint`, :meth:`sign_batch_with_checkpoint`,
915	    :meth:`sign_multiproof_with_checkpoint`,
916	    :meth:`sign_proof_with_checkpoint`,
917	    :meth:`sign_batch_proof_with_checkpoint`,
918	    :meth:`sign_with_auth_state`, :meth:`sign_batch_with_auth_state`,
919	    :meth:`sign_multiproof_with_auth_state`,
920	    :meth:`sign_proof_with_auth_state` or

922	    every leaf is spent, further calls raise :class:`KeyExhaustedError`.

925	    atomically recorded with :meth:`advance_to_with_auth_state`): after a
926	    crash or whenever state is uncertain, a caller skips leaves that may

929	    public way to move it backwards.

937	        token_bytes: Callable[[int], bytes] = secrets.token_bytes,

940	        height = _validate_height(height)

949	    def _init_state(

951	        w: int,
952	        height: int,

959	            level = layers[-1]

961	                [_node_hash(level[i], level[i + 1]) for i in range(0, len(level), 2)]
962	            )

964	        self._height = height
965	        self._private_keys = private_keys
